climate.about: The one climate under geology and weather (W7a): a diffusive energy balance in latitude and season (North 1975) with the moisture, cloud and wind it implies, plus the Held and Hou and Rhines numbers every reader shares. Surface wear and cover and both weather blocks read this and nothing else.

olr.source: Outgoing longwave linear in temperature, A + B T (Budyko 1969 eq. 1: I = a + B T - (a1 + B1 T) n with a 14.0, B 0.14, a1 3.0, B1 0.10 kcal cm-2 month-1, T in deg C). At cloudiness n 0.5 that is B = 1.43 W m-2 K-1 and 220 W m-2 at 288 K, so B T / (4 OLR) = 0.47 on Earth; the same dimensionless slope is used on every world (docs/fudges.md). A is set so the global mean temperature is the world's own.

diffusion.source: Diffusive heat transport D (1/cos phi) d/dphi (cos phi dT/dphi) (North 1975). D on Earth fitted to an equator-to-pole contrast near 40 K; scaling with air column and (Omega_Earth / Omega)^2 is a stand-in for eddy transport theory (docs/fudges.md).

ice.source: Ice-albedo step on water worlds, smoothed; edge and step fitted, base albedo renormalised so the world's Bond albedo is kept (docs/fudges.md).

heat_capacity.source: Seasonal energy balance with heat capacity, C dT/dt (North and Coakley 1979; North, Cahalan and Coakley 1981). C is the sea's mixed layer (about 50 m of water) over the sea fraction, the ground's seasonal skin, thermal inertia I times sqrt(year / pi) (Pierrehumbert 2010, ch. 7), over the land, plus the air column c_p p / g. One ground inertia (1500 SI, between dry regolith near 200 and wet rock near 2500) on every world until cover publishes it per cell (docs/fudges.md).

wind10.source: The 10 m wind is the circulation's prevailing wind plus storms as an isotropic Gaussian vector wind (Monahan 2006, J. Climate 19, 497): each component spreads by gust_share x the eddy wind x the eddies' share of the heat transport (1 - exp(-x^2/sigma^2), the moisture block's Hadley width), slower as the cube root of the air's density over Earth's. gust_share is fitted to Earth's storm-track spread of about 5 to 6 m/s: docs/fudges.md.

sea.source: Tides (sse.tides.ocean_range, sse.tides.period) and wind waves (sse.ocean.wind_waves, Coastal Engineering Manual eqs. II-2-36 and II-2-37). A wind's fetch is the band's open water between coasts, (1 - land) x the band's circumference / (coasts / 2), held to a storm's size of about 1000 km (synoptic storms span 1000 to 2000 km; one wind direction holds over a part of that): docs/fudges.md.

land_sea.source: W7c part 1: each band holds a land column and a sea column with their own heat capacities (North, Mengel and Short 1983 for land and sea in a seasonal energy balance). They share the band's meridional transport and exchange heat across the band's coasts by the model's own diffusion D: with n coasts around the band, nu = n^2 D / (4 pi^2 cos^2 phi) per square metre of band (blocks of land and sea alternating, heat crossing each coast from block centre to block centre). Two coasts (one continent per band) unless the world counts them (docs/fudges.md).

moisture.source: Bulk evaporation rho C_E |U| q_sat (1 - RH), capped by the energy reaching wet ground; C_E |U| fitted to Earth's mean rain (docs/fudges.md). Transport after Siler, Roe and Armour 2018 (J. Climate 31, 7481): eddies diffuse moisture down its gradient; the Hadley cell carries the share w = exp(-x^2/sigma^2) of the moist static energy flux (x = sin latitude, sigma 0.3 on Earth), and its lower branch carries moisture toward the equator, F_q = -F_HC L q / (h_T - h), h_T = 1.06 h at the equator. sigma scales with the world's own Hadley edge (our extension, docs/fudges.md).

cloud.source: Cloud from latent heat released and from baroclinic temperature gradients; frost cloud where a gas saturates at the band temperature. All constants fitted (docs/fudges.md).

supply.source: Energy-limited precipitation: the latent heat flux, a share of the sunlight reaching wet ground, falls back as liquid (Pierrehumbert 2010, ch. 9 energy budget). Sunlight reaching the ground falls with air column, fitted to Earth, Venus and Titan; cloud cover from latent flux fitted to Earth (docs/fudges.md).

circulation.source: Hadley edge from Held and Hou 1980 (small-angle form, phi_H = (5/3 g H dh / (Omega a)^2)^1/2); cells from the Rhines arrest wavenumber k = (beta/2U)^1/2, one cell pi/k wide, U the eddy speed (Rhines 1975); trends checked against Kaspi and Showman 2015. The wind scale comes from the thermal wind (W7b, strengths); the contrast is tuned to Earth (docs/fudges.md). The regime is a label read off the strengths and facts: the first rule whose conditions hold. The physics never reads it.

rules.because: The air is too thin to act as a fluid (Knudsen number above 1): an exosphere, no weather.
No surface under the air: belts and zones between alternating jets, storms and polar features (W3).
One face to the star: rising air and a permanent cloud shield under the star, clearer night side (Yang, Cowan and Abbot 2013; Showman and Polvani 2011).
Air so thin it heats and cools in days (radiative time under 10 days): thin ice cloud, frost, fog in basins and dust storms where there is dust (Zurek and Martin 1993).
Slow spin for the air's warmth (thermal Rossby number above about 1): one overturning cell reaches the pole and the upper air super-rotates (Mitchell and Vallis 2010; Held and Hou 1980).
Fast spin breaks each hemisphere into many narrow belts and jets (Rhines 1975; Kaspi and Showman 2015).
Moderate spin: a tropical cell, a mid-latitude storm track and a polar cell in each hemisphere.

strengths.source: Process strengths (W7b): thermal Rossby number and super-rotation onset near 1 (Mitchell and Vallis 2010; the strength curve's shape is ours); baroclinic growth 0.31 f dU/dz / N (Lindzen and Farrell 1980) against the radiative time c_p p/(g sigma T^3) (Koll and Abbot 2016); day-night contrast from the timescale ratio (Komacek and Showman 2016, eq. 31) with drag C_D a/H (Koll and Abbot 2016); collapse from the night side, no colder than Wordsworth 2015's thin radiator, against the main gas's frost point; collisional air from the Knudsen number; deformation and Rhines lengths against the radius (Haqq-Misra et al. 2018). Eddy share 0.4 fitted so Earth keeps three cells (docs/fudges.md).

tested.by: Mitchell and Vallis 2010 ran Ro_T 0.02 to 10.5
Komacek and Showman 2016 is a theory of hot Jupiters; on a world with a surface it is carried over
Wordsworth 2015 sampled 0.2 to 3 times Earth's sunlight
Haqq-Misra et al. 2018 covered synchronous rotators of about 1 to 100 days

water.source: Snow below freezing + 1.0 K, the mean 50% rain-snow threshold over 6883 Northern Hemisphere stations (Jennings et al. 2018). Air temperature scatters 5 K about a season's mean, the value of Calov and Greve 2005's Greenland example. Melt by positive degree days (Calov and Greve 2005), 8 mm per K per day on ice and 3.2 on snow (Braithwaite 1995: ice about 8, snow 36-44% of ice). Evaporation and runoff by Fu's Budyko curve, omega 2.6 (Zhang et al. 2004). Potential evaporation is the energy-limited flux of supply.latent_share (docs/fudges.md).

saltation.source: Fluid threshold of Shao and Lu 2000 (A_N 0.111, cohesion 2.9e-4 N/m from Kok and Renno 2006) as given by Kok et al. 2012; impact threshold 0.82 of it on Earth and about Earth's value in thin air (Kok 2010); law of the wall with z0 = D/30 (Kok et al. 2012); Weibull gusts k = 2 (Kok 2010); transport, once started by one ten-minute wind above the fluid threshold in a year or by lofting, runs while the wind is above the impact threshold (Kok 2010 hysteresis); grains lofted by subliming ice where the main gas freezes out (Telfer et al. 2018, Pluto: methane ice 494 kg/m3, 210-310 micron); dune activity by Lancaster's (1988) mobility index, inactive below 50 and fully active above 200. The ten-metre share (Earth's band winds of about 12 m/s to the observed 6-7 m/s over the sea), the gust share (Venus and Titan near 1 m/s at the ground) and its cube-root fall with air density, lofting width, the aridity floor and the grain by temperature are ours (docs/fudges.md).

rules.because: Snow outlasts the summer here, so ice builds up.
Almost nothing falls here.
Even the warmest season stays below freezing (Koppen EF).
The warmest season stays below 10 C (Koppen ET).
Rain is less than half of what the heat would dry (Koppen BW).
Rain is less than the heat would dry (Koppen BS).
Warm all year and wetter than evaporation can take (Koppen A; wet by P/PE rather than the driest month).
Warm all year with a dry spell (Koppen A).
Winters freeze below -3 C (Koppen D).
Mild winters between -3 C and 18 C (Koppen C).
Its liquid never thaws here.
Less falls than its liquid could evaporate.
More falls than its liquid can evaporate.

areas.source: Koppen-Geiger criteria of Kottek et al. 2006 (Table 1 and eq. 2.1), applied to each place's own temperatures and rain, after the ice balance (physics) and with plain labels for worlds whose liquid is not water. A label is read off the numbers; nothing reads it back.

forcing.source: Spin axis s' = alpha (n.s)(s x n), alpha = K (kappa + beta), K = (3/2) E_d GM/(omega a^3), kappa = (1-e^2)^-3/2, beta = g_L (a/a_L)^3 m_L/M (Zeebe 2022 eqs. 1-5; Earth E_d 0.00327381, Table 1). Summer energy over days of at least 275 W/m2 (Huybers 2006). E_d scaled as spin squared, g_L 1 (it reproduces Earth's 50.4 arcsec/yr with the Moon), the linear ice-balance response to summer energy, the 400 kyr window and the drawn sibling inclinations are ours (docs/fudges.md).

exchange.source: W8 part 2: frost pins the ground at the main gas's frost point (Fray and Schmitt 2009's curves on the master data sheet); latent heat from the curve's slope; the gas's partial pressure is its inventory less the ground's ice (vapour-pressure buffering, Bertrand and Forget 2016; Forget et al. 2017). Without ground ice the air is the inventory and the given mean pressure holds; with it, a year's change carries forward until a band would run out.
